title: Chapter 1 Quiz: Spring Boot Kickoff
description: Test your knowledge of Spring Boot basics, setup, and your first controller.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of Spring Boot?
options: Replace Java with a new language
Simplify the creation of production‑ready Spring applications
questions.explanation: Spring Boot’s main purpose is to reduce boilerplate configuration and provide a fast way to create production‑ready Spring applications.

questions.question: Spring Boot requires an external Tomcat server to run.
questions.explanation: Spring Boot includes an embedded Tomcat (or Jetty/Undertow) server, so you don't need to install one separately.

questions.question: Which annotation marks a class as a Spring Boot application?
questions.explanation: `@SpringBootApplication` is the main annotation that enables auto‑configuration and component scanning.

questions.question: Maven is the only build tool that Spring Boot supports.
questions.explanation: Spring Boot also works with Gradle. You can choose either at project creation.

questions.question: Which dependency is required to build a REST API?
questions.explanation: **Spring Web** provides the necessary classes (like `@RestController`, `@GetMapping`) to handle HTTP requests.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The main method of a Spring Boot application typically calls `________.run()`.
questions.explanation: `SpringApplication.run(YourApplication.class, args)` is the standard way to bootstrap the app.

questions.question: What does the `@RestController` annotation do?
options: Marks a class as a repository
Marks a class as a controller where every method returns data instead of a view
Marks a class as a configuration class
Marks a class as a component
questions.explanation: `@RestController` is a convenience annotation that combines `@Controller` and `@ResponseBody` – perfect for REST APIs.

questions.question: Spring Boot can only be used with Java 8 or earlier.
questions.explanation: Spring Boot 3.x requires Java 17 or later, but older versions of Spring Boot work with Java 8.

questions.question: Which file contains Maven dependencies for a Spring Boot project?
questions.explanation: Maven projects use `pom.xml` to declare dependencies, plugins, and project metadata.

questions.question: The `@GetMapping` annotation is a shortcut for `@RequestMapping(method = __________)`.
questions.explanation: `@GetMapping` is equivalent to `@RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.GET)`.

questions.question: You can change the server port by adding `server.port=9090` to `application.properties`.
questions.explanation: Yes, Spring Boot reads many configuration properties from `application.properties`, including `server.port`.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `@ComponentScan`?
options: Tells Spring where to look for components, services, and controllers
questions.explanation: `@ComponentScan` instructs Spring to discover beans in specified packages. It is included in `@SpringBootApplication`.

questions.question: The `main` method in a Spring Boot app is optional.
questions.explanation: The `main` method is the entry point that starts the embedded server and initializes the application context.

questions.question: Which tool can you use to generate a Spring Boot project from a web interface?
questions.explanation: **Spring Initializr** (start.spring.io) is the official web tool to bootstrap Spring Boot projects.

questions.question: The default path for static resources (like CSS, images) in a Spring Boot project is `src/main/resources/_______`.
questions.explanation: Spring Boot serves static content from `/static`, `/public`, `/resources`, and `/META-INF/resources` by default. The most common is `static`.

questions.question: What does the `@ResponseBody` annotation do?
options: Writes the return value of a method as the HTTP response body
Marks a class as a request body
Redirects the response to another URL
questions.explanation: `@ResponseBody` tells Spring to write the returned object directly to the HTTP response, not to resolve a view name.

questions.question: Spring Boot always uses Tomcat as the embedded server.
questions.explanation: Tomcat is the default, but you can switch to Jetty or Undertow by excluding the Tomcat starter and adding the appropriate one.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `SpringApplication.run()` method?
options: It starts the embedded server and boots the application
It creates a new Spring Boot project
questions.explanation: `SpringApplication.run()` launches the application, creates the `ApplicationContext`, and starts the embedded server.

questions.question: A class annotated with `@RestController` is automatically detected by Spring thanks to _______ scanning.
questions.explanation: Component scanning detects classes annotated with `@Component` (and its specializations like `@RestController`).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Spring Boot?
questions.explanation: Spring Boot does not provide a built‑in ORM for all databases; you add Spring Data JPA or other starters. It does provide auto‑configuration, embedded servers, and production features.
